question.text: In the comparative table of AIF structures (Table 8.1 of Chapter 8), which structure uses TWO pooling vehicles AND invests in domestic investee companies via BOTH the domestic AIF and directly from abroad?

explanation.text: The Logic: Table 8.1: Parallel has 2 pooling vehicles (onshore AIF + offshore fund), and both route investments into domestic investee companies — the AIF via Indian pooling and the offshore fund directly. Unified also has 2 vehicles but offshore commitments flow THROUGH the onshore AIF only. The Trap: Option A: 1 pooling vehicle, India. Option B: 1 vehicle, abroad. Option D: 2 vehicles but offshore flows into the onshore, not directly to investee. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C focuses heavily on this 4-way structure comparison — Table 8.1 is the go-to reference. Manager's Pro-Tip: Offshore LPs prefer parallel when a particular Indian deal is legally unsuitable for them (e.g., sector cap) — they can opt out of that deal in parallel vehicle, which is impossible in Master-Feeder.
